s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution
salient_findings: Intensely pruritic skin lesions on anterior thighs
Lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and purpuric edges
Symmetric, mirror-image distribution on anterior thighs
key_facts: 6-year-old girl with no relevant medical history
Lesions resolve spontaneously without residual injury
No preceding infection, topical exposures, sunburn, bites, animal contacts, or recent medications

raw.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution
salient_findings: Intensely pruritic skin lesions on anterior thighs
Lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and purpuric edges
Symmetric, mirror-image distribution on anterior thighs
key_facts: 6-year-old girl with no relevant medical history
Lesions resolve spontaneously without residual injury
No preceding infection, topical exposures, sunburn, bites, animal contacts, or recent medications

differentials: Perinatal lethal form of Gaucher disease
per_call: Perinatal lethal form of Gaucher disease

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, matching the patient's skin lesions

shortlist.label: Urticarial vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric edges and recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Lesions with central clearing and purpuric edges, although less common, can be seen in erythema multiforme

shortlist.label: Annular erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent, annular skin lesions with a similar morphology to the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric edges and the possibility of vasculitis, given the patient's presentation and negative serologies

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, central clearing, and purpuric edges, along with the recurrent and self-resolving nature of the lesions, is most consistent with Erythema annulare centrifugum.

rejected.label: Urticarial vasculitis
rejected.why: Laboratory studies were within normal limits, and there were no systemic symptoms or evidence of inflammation, making urticarial vasculitis less likely.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The lack of mucosal involvement, systemic symptoms, and negative serologies for infections make Erythema multiforme less likely.

rejected.label: Annular erythema
rejected.why: While the morphology of the lesions is similar, Annular erythema is a broader term, and Erythema annulare centrifugum is a more specific diagnosis that better fits the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory studies were within normal limits, and there was no evidence of inflammation or vasculitis on examination, making Leukocytoclastic vasculitis less likely.
